items.title: UN Ends Three Decades of Political Mission in Somalia
items.description: The closure of the U.N. Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) follows a two-year transition agreed with the federal government. Its responsibilities have been transferred to Somali institutions and U.N. agencies. The mission's roots dates back to 1995, when the U.N. established its Political Office for Somalia. It was replaced by the U.N. Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNSOM) in 2013 before entering its final transition phase as UNTMIS in 2024. items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said.
